sources.entry: GO Feature Flag - Simple, complete, and lightweight feature flag solution (alternative to LaunchDarkly). (Source Code) MIT Go

summary.one_liner: GO Feature Flag is a self-hosted, open-source feature flag solution usable as a Go module or through a relay proxy that serves OpenFeature SDKs in other languages.
summary.what_it_does: It lets you define feature flags in YAML, JSON or TOML files, with variations of type bool, int, float, string, JSON array or JSON object. Flag files can be loaded from sources such as local file, HTTP, S3, Kubernetes ConfigMaps, MongoDB, Redis and PostgreSQL. Targeting rules use a simple query expression language or JSONLogic, and rollouts support percentages, progressive, scheduled and experimentation (A/B) strategies. A relay proxy exposes an HTTP API so non-Go code can evaluate flags via OpenFeature providers. Flag evaluation events can be exported to destinations like S3, Kafka, BigQuery or OpenTelemetry, and change notifications can go to Slack, webhooks, Discord or Microsoft Teams.
use_cases: Roll out a feature to a percentage of users
Run A/B tests with feature flags
Toggle features per user with targeting rules
Serve feature flags to Go, Java, Python or JavaScript apps via a central proxy
Store and version flag configuration in a file or remote bucket
Export flag usage data for analytics
notable: Works as a Go module embedded in code or as a self-hosted relay proxy for multi-language use
Built on the OpenFeature standard with provider packages for many languages
Flag files can be stored in many backends including GitHub, GitLab, S3 and Kubernetes ConfigMaps
Companion GO Feature Flag Editor and CLI linter for writing and checking configs
caveats: Multi-language support depends on running the relay proxy as a separate service
OpenFeature is described as early stage, so some languages are unsupported and changes are expected
Only feature events are currently exported
keywords: manage flags without a backend server
